# Todoist for Personal Assistant Integration

## Personal Task Management via Claude API + MCP

Date: 2026-03-30

### Methodology

This analysis covers 5 research dimensions investigated via parallel sub-agents performing
independent web searches (iteration 1: discovery, iteration 2: deep analysis). Every factual
claim cites a numbered source from [citations.md](citations.md). Two independent audit agents
verified citations and cross-file consistency after writing. Reference files in
[references/](references/) contain full per-dimension findings.

### Core Question

Should the existing advisory PA (covering Jira, GitHub, Google Workspace, Slack, Claude)
add Todoist for personal task management, and if so, how?

---

## 1. Executive Summary

**Yes — Todoist is the right tool.** It has the best API quality, the only vendor-maintained
MCP server, the simplest authentication for single-user use, and a data model purpose-built
for personal task management [1][14][34].

Among alternatives (Trello, TickTick, Microsoft To Do), Todoist is the clear winner for PA
integration. Trello's kanban model is wrong for personal tasks [29]. TickTick's API is
described as "only very basic and not very useful" [28]. Microsoft To Do requires Azure AD
registration with a 7-step setup process [19].

| Decision | Recommendation |
|----------|---------------|
| Tool choice | Todoist [1][14] |
| MCP server | Official (ai.todoist.net/mcp) for hosted PA; greirson/mcp-todoist for self-hosted [14][15] |
| Auth approach | `data:read` OAuth scope for advisory mode [3] |
| Pricing tier | Pro recommended (~$5/mo) for reminders + filters [4] |
| Sync strategy | Sync API polling every 5-10 min [2] |
| Deduplication | Filter out "Todoist" calendar events from Google Calendar reads [5] |

---

## 2. Platform & API

### API Surface

Todoist exposes a comprehensive REST API at `/api/v1/` with full CRUD endpoints for tasks,
projects, sections, labels, comments, reminders, filters, user info, activity logs, and
backups [1]. The task object includes priority (1-4), due dates (date/datetime/timezone),
duration (amount + unit), labels, parent_id for subtasks, and assignee_id [1].

The `GET /api/v1/tasks` endpoint accepts a `filter` parameter using Todoist's filter syntax,
enabling queries like `(today | overdue)` or `p1 & 7 days` [1][7]. This is the most important
endpoint for an advisory PA.

A separate Sync API at `POST /api/v1/sync` adds batching (multiple operations per request),
incremental sync via `sync_token` (only modified data), and access to sync-only resources
like day orders and live notifications [2].

### Authentication

For a single-user advisory PA, a personal API token from Todoist's integration settings is
the simplest approach [3]. For production or multi-user scenarios, OAuth 2.0 with the
`data:read` scope restricts access to read-only operations [3].

### Rate Limits

REST: 1000 requests per 15-minute window per user [10][26]. Sync: 50 requests per minute, max
100 commands per request [2]. For an advisory PA polling every 5-10 minutes, this is
negligible — a briefing using 3 API calls hourly consumes 0.075% of the rate limit [10].

### Webhooks

Real-time notifications via HTTPS POST with HMAC-SHA256 verification for `item:added`,
`item:updated`, `item:deleted` events [3][27]. Requires a publicly accessible HTTPS endpoint,
which adds infrastructure for a local-first PA. Sync API polling is simpler for personal
use [2].

### Pricing

| Tier | Cost | PA-Critical Features |
|------|------|---------------------|
| Free | $0 | 5 projects, 3 filters, no reminders, no durations [4] |
| Pro | ~$5/mo (annual) | 300 projects, 150 filters, reminders, durations, calendar layout [4] |
| Business | ~$8/user/mo | Pro + team workspace, SOC2 [4] |

**Pro is recommended** for PA use. The Free tier's 3 filter views and lack of reminders
significantly limit what the PA can surface [4].

## 3. MCP Server Ecosystem

### Official: Doist/todoist-ai

Doist maintains an official MCP server at https://github.com/Doist/todoist-ai (409 stars,
TypeScript, actively maintained as of 2026-03-30) [14]. It provides a hosted streamable HTTP
endpoint at `https://ai.todoist.net/mcp` — no local server infrastructure needed [14].

Design philosophy: "Small set of tools that enable complete workflows, rather than just
atomic actions" [14]. Known tools include `findTasksByDate` and `addTasks`; the full set is
in the source code but not enumerated in the README [14].

Claude Code setup: `claude mcp add --transport http todoist https://ai.todoist.net/mcp` [14].

### Community: greirson/mcp-todoist

The most comprehensive community server at https://github.com/greirson/mcp-todoist (187 stars,
last pushed 2026-03-11) provides 19 MCP tools covering every Todoist resource type [15].
Notable features include bulk operations, subtask hierarchy management, activity logs,
completed task retrieval, and a dry-run mode (`DRYRUN=true`) for testing [15].

Auth uses a simple `TODOIST_API_TOKEN` environment variable [15].

### Which to Use?

| Scenario | Recommendation | Rationale |
|----------|---------------|-----------|
| Hosted PA, production use | Official (ai.todoist.net) | Maintained by Doist, OAuth, no infrastructure [14] |
| Self-hosted, full control | greirson/mcp-todoist | 19 tools, API token auth, dry-run [15] |
| Read-only advisory | Either | Use `data:read` OAuth scope [3] |

No MCP server implements a `--read-only` flag, but OAuth scope enforcement at the API level
provides read-only guarantees regardless of server [3][14][15].

## 4. PA Integration Design

### What to Surface

The PA should query Todoist to surface personal task signals alongside work signals
from Jira, GitHub, Google Workspace, and Slack:

| Priority | Signal | Query |
|----------|--------|-------|
| High | Overdue personal tasks | `filter=overdue` [7] |
| High | Today's personal tasks | `filter=today` [7] |
| High | High-priority items due soon | `filter=p1 & 7 days` [7] |
| Medium | Upcoming deadlines | `filter=7 days` [7] |
| Low | Recurring tasks due today | `filter=today & recurring` [7] |

### Efficient Polling

A daily briefing requires 2-3 API calls:

1. `GET /api/v1/tasks?filter=(today | overdue)` — everything needing attention [1][7]
2. `GET /api/v1/tasks?filter=7 days & p1` — upcoming high-priority [1][7]
3. `GET /api/v1/user/productivity_stats` — completion trends [1]

Even hourly polling at 3 calls/hour uses 72 requests/day — 1.8% of the daily capacity [10].

### Data Model Integration

The PA maps Todoist concepts to its unified action list:

```
Todoist Task (p1, overdue, #Home)
  → PA Action Item {
      source: "todoist",
      priority: "high",        // from p1
      context: "Home",         // from project
      categories: ["errands"], // from labels
      due: "2026-03-29",       // overdue
      status: "overdue"
    }
```

### Architecture

Todoist becomes the 6th MCP data source in the existing PA architecture:

```
Claude API ◄──► MCP Clients ──► Todoist API (personal tasks)
                              ├──► Jira API (work tasks)
                              ├──► GitHub API (code activity)
                              ├──► Google WS API (calendar, email)
                              └──► Slack API (messages)
```

The key distinction: **Jira tracks work tasks; Todoist tracks personal tasks.** These are
separate domains with no overlap in the PA's unified view.

## 5. Alternatives Comparison

| Criterion | Todoist | Trello | TickTick | Microsoft To Do |
|-----------|--------|--------|----------|-----------------|
| API quality | Best — REST + Sync, filter syntax [1][2] | Good — REST, mature [20] | Limited — "basic" [28] | Complex — Graph API [23] |
| Auth setup | Minutes (API token) [3] | Minutes (key + token) [21] | Medium (OAuth2) [22] | Hours (Azure AD) [19] |
| MCP server | 409★ official + 187★ community [14][15] | 287★ [18] | None notable | 49★, stale [19] |
| Data model fit | Purpose-built for tasks [34] | Kanban boards [25] | Similar to Todoist [28] | Basic lists [33] |
| Read-only | data:read scope [3] | scope=read [21] | tasks:read [32] | Tasks.Read [19] |
| Price (paid) | ~$5/mo [4] | ~$5/mo [24] | ~$3/mo [43] | Free [33] |
| Integrations | 80+ [26] | Mature ecosystem [18] | Limited [28] | MS ecosystem [33] |

**Todoist wins** on API quality, MCP ecosystem, and data model fit. TickTick's only
advantage (habit tracking) comes with an impractical API. Microsoft To Do is free but
the Azure AD setup complexity and stale MCP server make it a poor PA candidate [19][23].

## 6. Sync & Interoperability

### Google Calendar

Todoist's 2-way calendar sync creates events on a dedicated "Todoist" calendar [5]. Task
changes (name, date, time, duration) propagate to calendar events [5]. Limitations: new
calendar events do not create Todoist tasks, single recurring event instances don't sync
back, and complex recurrences are unsupported [5].

**PA deduplication**: Filter out events from the "Todoist" calendar when reading Google
Calendar data. Todoist is the authoritative source for personal tasks; the calendar mirror
is for user convenience, not PA consumption [5].

### Slack

The `/todoist` slash command creates tasks with due dates, labels, and project names [6].
Messages can be converted to tasks via the three-dot menu [6]. Limitations: single
workspace only, individual account setup [6].

**PA impact**: Slack integration is write-side only (creates tasks in Todoist). The PA
reads from Todoist directly, so there's no read-side duplication from Slack [6].

### Automation Platforms

Todoist integrates with Zapier (1000+ apps), n8n (150+ apps), and IFTTT [36][37][38].
The user's PA already includes n8n research, making n8n a natural bridge for any
automation workflows between Todoist and other PA data sources [37][39].

### Recurring Tasks

When completed, recurring tasks reset with the next occurrence date and log the completion
in Activity — they don't disappear [8]. The PA will see recurring tasks "reappear" with
new due dates. Completed instances are retrievable via
`GET /api/v1/tasks/completed_by_completion_date` [1].

### Real-Time Options

For a local-first PA, **Sync API polling every 5-10 minutes** is recommended over webhooks.
Webhooks require a public HTTPS endpoint, adding infrastructure complexity [2][27]. Sync
API polling at 5-minute intervals uses 12 requests/hour — well within the 50/min limit [2].

## 7. Implementation Path

### Phase 1: Read-Only Advisory (Week 1-2)

1. Get a Todoist Pro subscription (~$5/mo) [4]
2. Generate a personal API token from Todoist integration settings [3]
3. Add the official MCP server: `claude mcp add --transport http todoist https://ai.todoist.net/mcp` [14]
4. Or use greirson's community server for granular tools: `claude mcp add todoist -e TODOIST_API_TOKEN=<token> -- npx @greirson/mcp-todoist` [15]
5. Add Todoist briefing queries to the PA prompt

### Phase 2: Deduplication (Week 2-3)

1. Configure Google Calendar integration in Todoist [5]
2. Add deduplication logic: skip events from the "Todoist" calendar when reading Google Calendar
3. Test with Sync API polling at 5-minute intervals [2]

### Phase 3: Write Capability (Optional, Week 3-4)

1. Upgrade OAuth scope to include `task:add` [3]
2. Enable quick_add for natural language task creation from PA [1][15]
3. Test with greirson's dry-run mode first (`DRYRUN=true`) [15]

---

## 8. Risks and Mitigations

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|------------|
| Free tier too limited | High | Pro subscription (~$5/mo) [4] |
| Duplicate signals (Calendar + Todoist) | Medium | Filter "Todoist" calendar events [5] |
| Official MCP tool set too narrow | Low | Use greirson's 19-tool server [15] |
| API version migration (v2 → v1) | Low | Both path prefixes likely active during transition [1] |
| Rate limit hit | Very Low | Advisory PA uses <2% of capacity [10] |
